rules.title: Bare except (no 'on E: ... do') catches every exception, even EOutOfMemory -- catch a specific exception class.
Case label is a literal -- consider naming the constant
Comparing ClassName to a string literal is fragile -- use 'is' or InheritsFrom().
Unreachable code after Exit/raise/Break/Continue/Halt
Both operands of this comparison are identical -- the result is constant; likely a typo.
Condition is always the same constant -- likely dead code or a logic error.
Exit/Break/Continue/Halt inside a finally block
Critical section acquired without a matching Leave/Release/TMonitor.Exit in finally
Division/modulo by a literal zero -- always raises a runtime division error.
Two 'on <Class>' handlers for the same class in one try -- the second is unreachable
Empty case branch -- the label has no statement (forgotten body, or add a comment if intentional).
Empty then/else branch is a no-op -- likely a stray ';' after 'then'/'else'.
Empty except block silently swallows every exception -- log it or re-raise.
Empty finally block does nothing -- remove it, or release the resource it was meant to free.
Empty loop body -- a stray ';' after 'do', or a busy-wait that should sleep/yield.
Empty exception handler ('on ... do ;') silently swallows the exception -- log it or re-raise.
Empty procedure/function body
A bare name inside a with body names an enum value AND a member of the with-target -- the compiler binds the member, drag-lint's index records the enum value
Exception E...Create(...) constructed as a statement but never raised
case on an enum type omits some members and has no else (store-aware; same-file enums covered without a DB)
Floating-point value compared with =
Format() argument count does not match the specifiers
Format() specifier type does not match the literal argument
Unit-level global variable of the form class type -- potential leak
IfThen() evaluates both branches unconditionally -- side effects in either argument always execute. Use if/then/else instead.
Integer literal -- consider naming the constant
Length(s) compared to 0 -- use s = '' / s <> ''
Loop body starts with Exit/Break/raise -- runs at most once
Ansi-narrowing cast of a Unicode string -- characters outside the code page are lost (W1057)
Constructor without an inherited call
Destructor without an inherited call
Prefer Assigned(X) over 'X = nil' / 'X <> nil' -- clearer, and correct for method-pointer references.
'not A = B' parses as '(not A) = B' -- likely a bug; write 'not (A = B)'.
'not X in S' parses as '(not X) in S' -- almost certainly a bug; write 'not (X in S)'.
'for I := 0 to X.Count/Length(X)' runs one past the end -- use 'to X.Count - 1' (or 'to High(X)').
Syntax error: parser failed to recognize this construct
A property's read/write accessor is the property itself -- infinite recursion
Raising the root Exception class -- raise a specific subclass so callers can handle it selectively.
raise inside a finally block masks the in-flight exception
The same condition repeats in an if/else-if chain -- the later branch is unreachable
'raise E;' resets the stack trace -- use a bare 'raise;' to re-raise and preserve the original origin.
'X := X' is a no-op self-assignment -- likely a copy-paste error.
Sleep() on the main thread freezes the VCL UI. Use TTimer for delays or TThread.Sleep in a background thread.
Destructive act gated on a file-existence check (a failed stat answers False)
String compared with = -- consider SameText/SameStr semantics
Source has a syntax error
try..except swallows the exception (no raise/log)
UI access inside a TThread.Execute (not thread-safe)
Unbalanced begin/end
Hard cast TFoo(x) of an object reference with no guarding 'x is TFoo'

UpperCase/LowerCase(...) compared to a string literal allocates a new string on every evaluation -- SameText compares in place and is clearer. (The literal's case agrees with the conversion here, so the comparison is correct; a literal in the OPPOSITE case is reported separately as uppercase-compare-always-false.)

UpperCase/LowerCase(...) compared to a literal in the opposite case -- the two can NEVER be equal, so '=' is always False and '<>' always True. Correct the literal's case to match the conversion (or use SameText if a case-insensitive match was intended).
Virtual/dynamic method called from a constructor
A bare name inside a with body binds to the with-target while an outer scope declares the same name -- the compiler never warns
Boolean expression has more than N and/or/xor operators
case has fewer than N branches -- an if is clearer
Cognitive complexity is too high (nesting-weighted)
Cyclomatic complexity is too high
Nesting is too deep
Duplicated code block detected (Type-2, renamed-identifier tolerant)
Routine body is too long
Routine has too many Exit statements
Routine has too many local variables
Routine has too many parameters
Unit exceeds N source lines
Object freed twice on a path with no reassignment between (double free)
Function Result not assigned on every path
Loop variable used after the loop
Interface variable dereferenced before assignment (nil interface call)
Created object may leak (not freed on every path)
out parameter not assigned on every path
Value overwritten before it is read
Variable used before assignment
Local assigned but never read
Redundant comparison with boolean literal (use the expression directly)
Redundant if/else assigning True/False to Result. Write 'Result := <cond>' (or 'Result := not <cond>') directly.
Comment appears to be commented-out code (assignment or call)
Result of a same-unit function call is discarded
then and else branches are identical
Redundant 'as TObject' cast - every Delphi object is already a TObject
Cast of a value to the type it already has (no-op)
Double negation 'not not X' -- simplify to X.
Redundant parentheses around a single term or nested parens
Private field is read but never assigned
Local variable is never used
Parameter is never used
DocInsight comment has drifted from the code it documents (--fix repairs the mechanically-safe subset)
Managed facts block is attached to no declaration -- a previous --apply stacked it above an existing block
A <param> tag is present but has no description -- the parameter's meaning is still undocumented
A <param> tag names a parameter the routine does not declare
Public declaration has no DocInsight doc-comment
Dataset opened without a matching Close in finally
FieldByName called inside a loop -- cache the field
Open vs ExecSQL does not match the SQL kind
Class inheritance is too deep (DIT)
Class is referenced by too many other classes (afferent coupling Ca)
Class depends on too many other classes (efferent coupling Ce; aliases CBO)
Class is coupled to too many other classes (CBO)
Class response set is too large (RFC)
Class instability (I=Ce/(Ca+Ce)) is high -- unstable: depends on many, nothing depends on it
Class methods lack cohesion (LCOM4)
Class has too many direct subclasses (NOC)
Two declarations differ only by underscores
Constant name casing
Field name must carry the configured prefix
Short or Hungarian-prefixed identifier
Local variable wears the field/param prefix
Local variable name casing
Method/routine name casing
Parameter name must carry the configured prefix
Reserved words must be lowercase
Type name must carry the configured prefix
Unit name must equal the file base name
Assert without a message argument -- add a second argument describing the failure.
TODO/FIXME/HACK comment -- track in issue tracker
S := S + X inside a loop is O(n^2) -- each '+' allocates a new string. Accumulate with TStringList or use string.Join.
Bare 'inherited' call - verify it invokes the intended ancestor method
OutputDebugString -- debug output left in code; remove it or guard with {$IFDEF DEBUG}.
Direct WriteLn call -- consider a logger.
File I/O (LoadFromFile/SaveToFile, TFile.*, TStreamReader/Writer) with no explicit TEncoding -- defaults to ANSI/locale
Obsolete RTL routine. Prefer TEncoding / modern string APIs.
GetTickCount wraps after ~49.7 days -- use GetTickCount64 for elapsed-time calculations.
Inline asm block -- not portable across compilers/platforms; prefer Pascal where possible.
Locale-sensitive conversion without a TFormatSettings -- behaves differently per regional settings; pass an explicit TFormatSettings.
NativeInt/pointer-sized value cast to a 32-bit integer type -- truncates on Win64
Pointer arithmetic on PChar -- unsafe and platform-specific (pointer size differs Win32/Win64). Use PChar[N] or string APIs.
SizeOf(Pointer) compared to a literal -- breaks on Win32 vs Win64. Guard with {$IFDEF WIN64} or compare to SizeOf of a platform-aware type.
Unsafe PChar string routine -- no length bound. Use System.AnsiStrings or TStringHelper equivalents.
Pointer cast to a 32-bit integer type -- unsafe on Win64
A routine with a PROVEN effect (writes a field, a global, a parameter or frees storage) is called inside Assert -- release builds compile Assert out, so the effect happens in Debug only
Circular unit dependency (a uses-graph cycle among project units)
This unit is one of the units of a circular unit dependency -- the per-unit view of circular-uses, pointing at `cycles --plan`
A dl:shared unit was changed after another project that also compiles it last built -- that project still holds object code for the older text
A .dfm sets a property that the component's class and its ancestors do not declare -- the form fails to load or silently drops the setting
A proven effect-free value-returning routine is called in statement position and its result discarded -- the call does nothing

The same name is declared at interface unit level in two or more units -- const, var, type, record, class, interface, enum or routine -- so which one compiles depends on uses order; or a project global that ALSO exists in a library unit the declaring file uses (masking an RTL name -- almost always a naming error; no autofix, a refactoring tool knows which one you meant)
Enum helper (record/class helper) is declared in a different unit than its target enum -- consider co-locating
A global variable is the ONLY link from one unit to another -- relocating it (or injecting it, when it is interface-typed) deletes the uses edge
Class has too many members/responsibilities
IFDEF/IFNDEF/defined() tests a symbol no build of the project defines -- dead branch, usually a typo
Interface reference cycle (ARC leak)
Unit dependency crosses an architectural layer
A Get*/Is*/Has*/Find*/Can*/Should* routine has a PROVEN escaping effect (writes a field, global state or frees storage) -- a question that also changes something
Unit is referenced but not listed in the .dpr
Private member is never referenced
Public symbol is never referenced
Unit in uses is never referenced
Used unit resolves to no known unit (project/library/alias)
How many of a used unit's globals and consts this unit actually draws, against how many that unit declares -- acknowledge a travels-together pair with // dl:unit <unit> accepted
Boolean flag parameter selects behavior -- consider splitting the routine
Method accesses another class more than its own -- Move Method closer to the data it uses
Loop exit driven by a boolean flag -- consider Break
Unexplained numeric literal -- extract a named constant
Message chain too long -- consider Hide Delegate
Class mostly delegates to one field -- Remove Middle Man (inline or expose the delegate)
Mutable global variable -- shared mutable state (Fowler Global Data)
Public class field -- expose via a property instead
Same case-selector repeated across 3+ methods -- Replace Conditional with Polymorphism (project-wide)
Value-returning function also mutates state -- Command-Query Separation violation; split into a pure query and a command
Local reused for two unrelated purposes (disjoint lifetimes) -- Split Variable into two locals
TFoo.Create on a class with an unimplemented abstract method -- raises EAbstractError (store-backed)
Object constructed as the first statement inside its try..finally -- construct before the try
Destructor not declared 'override' -- hides the inherited destructor (leak)
FreeAndNil on an interface reference
Object aliased into an interface AND manually freed in the same routine -- dual-handle double-free risk
'if Assigned(X) then X.Free' -- the guard is redundant; Free and FreeAndNil already handle nil.
Object created + freed without try-finally
Object used after X.Free
dl:ok names something that is not a rule id -- the marker suppresses nothing
dl:ok carries a placeholder or malformed @hash (e.g. @0000) -- it suppresses nothing; re-record it with `allow`
dl:ok reason has no REVIEWED <yyyy-mm-dd> stamp, or it is older than max_age_days -- re-read the reason and re-stamp it
dl:ok marker no longer matches the line it reviews -- the finding is reported again; re-review and re-mark
dl:ok marker records a finding that no longer occurs -- remove the marker
A credential-named DFM property (Password/Secret/ApiKey) holds a literal string

A hardcoded ABSOLUTE root -- a drive letter or a UNC lead. A COMPLETE path reaching a file/directory/ini/dataset-location sink reports at warning; a bare root at info; a literal reaching NO modelled sink at info, for review (a relative path and a bare file name + extension are allowed)
Hardcoded connection string -- embeds credentials / environment coupling (CWE-798); load it from config.
Hardcoded credential -- a secret-like const is set to a string literal (CWE-798); load it from config/secret store.
Hardcoded IP address -- ties the code to one host/network; read it from config.
File written to a hardcoded temp path (\Temp\, C:\Temp) -- predictable/insecure location
Concatenated path passed to a file API -- path traversal risk
SQL string concatenated with a variable -- SQL injection risk (CWE-89); use a parameterized query.
A command line built at runtime: WinExec/CreateProcess with a non-literal command, or ShellExecute with runtime parameters, a non-plain verb, or an interpreter as lpFile
A security-named variable is generated with System.Random (not a CSPRNG)
goto statement is generally considered harmful
Inline comment inside a multi-line argument list
Two or more statements share one source line
Nested with statement (scope highly ambiguous)
Public field on a class breaks encapsulation -- expose it via a property.
'with A, B do' lists multiple objects -- name resolution is highly ambiguous; use explicit qualified access.
'with' statement makes symbol scope ambiguous
